newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr firms to 1.64 marks, mark/yen eases in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr firms to 1.64 marks, mark/yen eases in Tokyo.

text.p: *Dollar rises to 1.64 mark level in afternoon trade in response to mark sales against yen in cross trade, while dollar/yen trapped in boxed range, dealers said.
*"The mark eased against the yen after the mark's rise was capped at 74.50 yen, which in turn helped firm the dollar against the mark," said a bank dealer.
*Dollar briefly firmed against yen in early afternoon Tokyo, mainly due to short-covering and talk of option-linked dollar buying. But offers stayed intact at around 122.30 yen, dealers said.
*Talk of offers by Japanese computer game maker at around 122.30 yen.
*But bank dealer said many Japanese exporters in no rush to sell dollar, despite fact they can sell dollars above 120 yen through forward contracts covering end of May.

*Expectations that Group of Seven (G7) nations unlikely to call for reversal of strong dollar trend at meeting in Berlin keeping dollar's bottom solid, with many traders quick to cover their short positions.
*"It will be difficult to hold on to dollar short positions before the G7 meeting," said the bank dealer.

*Dollar inched up against yen by midday Tokyo on Tuesday, hovering near 122 yen, partly on buying of marks and sterling for yen in crosses and reports that Japanese hotel operator faces bankruptcy, dealers said.
*Although profit-taking and some offers from exporters weighed on dollar, clear break over 122.25-30 yen level could signal further gains, a trust bank dealer said.
* "Buying of marks and sterling for the yen was supporting the dollar against the Japanese currency," a city bank dealer said.
